text: "Me at the zoo" is the first video uploaded to YouTube on April 23, 2005, at 8:27 p.m. (UTC−7), and is recognized as the platform's inaugural upload. The 19-second video was recorded by Jawed Karim’s high school friend, Yakov Lapitsky, and features Karim standing in front of two elephants at the San Diego Zoo in California, where he comments on the length of their trunks, saying: "Alright, so here we are in front of the, uh, elephants, and the cool thing about these guys is that, is that they have really, really, really long, um, trunks, and that's, that's cool. And that's pretty much all there is to say." YouTube was founded in 2005 by Chad Hurley, Steve Chen, and Jawed Karim, with Hurley studying design at the Indiana University of Pennsylvania and Chen studying computer science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Karim was inspired to create the platform after being unable to find video clips of the Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy and the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami online. Multiple journalists and publications have recognized the video as a milestone in YouTube's history, with Business Insider, The New York Observer, and BuzzFeed News ranking it as one of the most important YouTube videos, and it has been described as the first YouTube vlog. Reviewers have noted that its ordinary, amateur nature set the tone for user-generated content and established an era of short videos, with Aaron Duplantier and the Los Angeles Times highlighting its significance in media consumption. Greg Jarboe described the video as "extraordinary" for its time, emphasizing that it reflected Karim’s vision of empowering users to become "broadcasters of tomorrow," which helped YouTube grow into the world's most popular online video-sharing community. The official San Diego Zoo YouTube account left a now-pinned comment in 2020 stating, “We're so honored that the first ever YouTube video was filmed here!”, which became the most-liked comment on the platform by April 1, 2025, with 4.2 million likes. Karim has repeatedly updated the video’s description to express criticism of YouTube’s business decisions, including in November 2013 when he stated, "I can't comment here anymore, since I don't want a Google+ account," and in November 2021 when he wrote, "When every YouTuber agrees that removing dislikes is a stupid idea, it probably is. Try again, YouTube," followed by a longer condemnation. On December 16, 2023, the video’s thumbnail was changed to a MrBeast-style image of Karim with fiery eyes and pointing at stampeding elephants, but it was reverted two weeks later. In February 2025, Karim updated the description to include a statement about the danger of microplastics to the brain. The description also includes timestamps for chapters: "Intro", "The cool thing", and "End". As of January 2026, the video has received more than 379 million views.
